applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union: freedom of establishment (Articles 49-55) and free movement of capital (Article 63)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (including the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing EU Directive 2015/849 and EU Directive 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs or RBE), as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (SCSp introduced by the 2016 company-law modernisation and codified in Articles 23 ff.; SCSp has no separate legal personality, so UBO piercing must reach through the general partner and every limited partner); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT, as amended; CSSF AML/CFT Circular 18/698, as updated by Circular 20/744; Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies; applicable Grand-Ducal regulations implementing the RBE and AML supervisory framework.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RBE is not fully public; direct public access requires a demonstrated legitimate-interest review by the Luxembourg Business Registers, consistent with CJEU joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; competent authorities, the financial intelligence unit, notaries, and AML-obliged entities retain full access)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each corporate entity in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the state of formation (e.g., Delaware Secretary of State, Companies House UK, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; for non-Hague Convention states, consular legalization through the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or constitutional equivalent of each intermediate holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporations registry of the jurisdiction of formation of each shareholder or limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable to the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport (full notarized copy) of each ultimate natural-person beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the UBO's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy certified by a competent notary, then Hague Apostille if the notarial act is issued outside the EU; non-Latin passports must be accompanied by a sworn French or English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill, regulated bank statement, or lease agreement issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, regulated credit institution, or landlord in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the source document originates outside the EU

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming commercial profile, source of funds, and integrity of the principal contributor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Existing regulated bank or financial institution of the UBO or contributing partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original signed by an authorized bank officer; notarization of the signature required if requested by the receiving AML-obliged entity; consular legalization required for banks in non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney nominating the general partner (gérant) and local filing representative to effect RCS and RBE filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary if executed as a notarial deed, or any signatory sworn before a civil-law notary in the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Luxembourg internal legalization when notarial; otherwise Hague Apostille from the executing state; LuxTrust electronic signature accepted for LBR e-filings

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, including Article 1 and Articles 143–154 (limited partnerships), and as supplemented by the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Agreement (Acte de Société / Contrat de Société) filed electronically with the RCS; publication extract lodged in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an SCSp; no statutory escrow account requirement applies. Partner capital commitments and contribution obligations are defined exclusively in the limited partnership agreement and are documented in the partner capital accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company, acting as corporate general partner, hereby: (i) approves the executed Limited Partnership Agreement of the SCSp in the form attached; (ii) subscribes for the general partner interest as provided therein, acknowledging that no minimum paid-up capital applies under the 1915 Law; (iii) adopts the registered office at the address stated in the Limited Partnership Agreement and authorises the domiciliation agreement with the registered office agent; (iv) appoints the named individual as Manager of the SCSp with sole signature authority for the term set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement; (v) appoints the Tax Compliance Officer and instructs counsel to file the RCS registration, beneficial owner declaration and VAT registration in a timely manner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Corporate Name and Verify RCS Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Online Portal at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the LBR online portal using the proposed SCSp name and required legal-form suffix. Confirm that the name is not confusingly similar to any existing RCS-registered entity. Use the official legal form designation 'SCSp' or 'S. C. Sp.' in the company name. No notarisation is required for a private SCSp. The name reservation is valid for one month and may be renewed once.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of the applicant
Power of attorney if filed by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of a conflict, promptly file a revised list of alternative names with the RCS. A judicial appeal may be brought before the Luxembourg District Court within 15 days of the refusal where the applicant asserts priority or legitimate interest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners and counsel; optional notary in case of a public offering or where notarial form is preferred
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp limited partnership agreement in French or German, with an English execution copy when required by investors. The agreement must identify at least one general partner with unlimited liability and at least one limited partner, define capital commitments, management powers, transfer restrictions, dissolution events and profit-sharing rules, and be governed by Luxembourg law. Execute the agreement by the partners or their lawfully appointed representatives. For a private placement, private writing is sufficient; for a public offering, notarial deed and publication requirements apply.
required_dossiers: Passports or IDs of all partners
AML/KYC files prepared by the domiciliation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registry or authority determines that notarial form is required, have the agreement executed before a Luxembourg notary and re-publish the notarial extract in the RCS application. Any defective clause may be cured by a written amendment deed signed by all partners and filed as a supplementary document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Domiciliation Agent and Adopt Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal authorities of the commune where the registered office is located; Luxembourg-licensed domiciliation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conclude a written domiciliation contract with a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent to obtain a registered office address. The agent must provide a formal attestation of domiciliation that identifies the SCSp and the registered office address and states that the address is available for official filings. Submit the attestation together with the RCS registration application. This stage also confirms the registered office for tax and VAT purposes.
required_dossiers: Attestation of domiciliation issued by the approved agent
Licence number and approval evidence of the domiciliation agent
Consent of the entity providing the premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the domiciliation attestation is insufficient or rejected, obtain a corrected attestation from the existing agent or engage an alternative licensed domiciliation provider and file the revised document without further delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for Registration with the RCS and Obtain RCS Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via the LBR electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RCS electronic application form on the LBR portal. Upload the executed SCSp limited partnership agreement, the domiciliation attestation, proof of identity of the manager and partners, and the signature specimen form. Pay the official filing fee by the available online method. Upon approval, the RCS issues the registration number and the corporate reference number linked to the Luxembourg social security registration.
required_dossiers: Passports or national IDs of manager and partners
Certified signature specimen of the manager
Proof of payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises an administrative query, address the identified deficiencies in writing through the LBR platform within the stated grace period, generally 10 business days. If the query is not resolved, re-file the corrected application and pay any incremental fee if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish in RESA and File Beneficial Owner Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RESA electronic gazette; Register of Beneficial Owners – RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the mandatory publication extract with the RESA electronic official gazette within one month after RCS registration. Then within the same statutory deadline, submit the RBE declaration identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly owns or controls more than 25% of the SCSp interests or exercises control over the partnership. The declaration must be kept updated.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS notifies a mismatch between the RESA extract and the RCS registration, supply a corrected extract and cancel the erroneous publication. If the RBE filing is late or inaccurate, submit a remedial declaration and provide reasoned justification to the RBE; penalties may be reduced or waived in cases of good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax and Administrative Filings, Including Any Business Establishment Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Ministry of the Economy where a commercial establishment permit is triggered
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Luxembourg VAT on the online VAT platform using Form 102 if taxable SaaS subscriptions will be supplied. Register the SCSp for social security purposes with the CCSS if employees are hired. Assess whether a business establishment permit under the Law of 2 September 2011 is required. For a pure SEO content analytics software tool delivered over the internet from an administrative office, no industrial or environmental permit applies; if the scope later includes physical office operations only, obtain the standard municipal and occupational clearances and, if commercial activity is found, apply to the Ministry of the Economy for an autorisation d'établissement.
required_dossiers: CCSS employee declaration if personnel engaged
Domiciliation contract and registered office confirmation
Business permit application form if applicable
Product and service description for the Ministry of the Economy if queried
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or economic authority questions the activity status, submit the SaaS agreements, product screenshots and technical documentation proving the absence of physical industrial manufacturing. Where a permit is required, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Minister within three months of the refusal or silent refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not required for pure MarTech Analytics SaaS. If a physical industrial site were later established, the competent authority would be the Ministry of the Economy, Directorate General for Industry.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit is required for a cloud-based SEO keyword analytics tool; the activity does not trigger an industrial establishment licence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based software analytics activity has no industrial installation under the Law of 21 March 2012 on environmental impact assessment; no EIA screening or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC or discharge thresholds apply to the administrative software activity. Any future server or data-processing facility must comply with the EU energy efficiency directive and Luxembourg climate legislation, and e-waste disposal must follow the WEEE directive.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must obtain standard fire safety certification in accordance with communal fire regulations if the premises are physically occupied. Structural load inspections apply only if server racks or heavy equipment are installed. The occupational health and safety clearance of the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines) requires a documented risk assessment, first-aid organisation, and a safe office environment for any staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDV) for VAT; central filing portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) and RCS registration via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first file incorporation documents and register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via a certified filing intermediary or notary if capital is introduced. Following RCS registration, the entity obtains a 13-digit national identification number (matricule) from the Luxembourg State Register. For VAT purposes, the entity must file a VAT registration form (Formulaire 300 / 400 VAT) with the AEDV, providing the matricule, registered office address, activity description, and supporting constitutional documents. Non-resident entities acting through no local establishment must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative for VAT if required by the AEDV. Income tax registration is effected through the ACD upon receipt of the matricule and may require a specific direct tax file reference for partnership returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is statutorily tax-transparent under Luxembourg direct tax law; no general check-the-box election exists analogous to the US, but may be regarded as a hybrid entity under foreign tax election rules, triggering Luxembourg anti-hybrid (ATAD) analysis. The partners may align fiscal treatment through partnership agreement allocations subject to Luxembourg substance and arm's-length principles. No corporate income tax election is available to a transparent SCSp.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 25,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-enterprise exemption; no registration threshold applies to non-established foreign entities, intra-EU acquisitions, or supplies of electronically supplied services to non-taxable EU persons, which trigger mandatory Luxembourg VAT registration or OSS/MOSS use
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G electronic invoicing through the Luxembourg government e-invoicing platform (Peppol / Factur-X) for public procurement; no general real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API clearance regime exists for B2B invoices. Traditional VAT invoices remain valid; e-invoicing is optional in B2B under private agreement, subject to authenticity-of-origin and integrity-of-content requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies when goods leave Luxembourg/EU customs territory in an export transaction evidenced by the Single Administrative Document (SAD) and received by a customer outside the EU. The supplier must prove the physical removal from the EU within the statutory time frame, hold transport and title-transfer documentation, and maintain an export declaration. Intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered customers may also be zero-rated under article 38 of the Luxembourg VAT law if the customer supplies a valid EU-VAT identification number and the goods are dispatched to another Member State. Offshore services, including SaaS and SEO analytics digital services, fall under the B2B general place-of-supply rule: if the customer is a taxable business outside Luxembourg/EU, the place of supply is outside Luxembourg, and the supply is outside the VAT scope; if the customer is an EU/global taxable person, the supply is taxable at the customer's jurisdiction under reverse-charge, and Luxembourg zero-rating/refund treatment may require supporting professional-services documentation and service recipient VAT status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document, SAD) for goods exports
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport evidence
Purchase order and contract of sale
Proof of payment / bank transfer records (often including inward remittance certificate, where available)
Certification of the receiving entity's non-EU status or EU VAT number for intra-EU supplies
Proof of delivery to non-EU destination (POD, warehouse records, or customs clearing agent report)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities apply Article 84 and related provisions of the law of 17 February 2012: failure to substantiate export zero-rating gives rise to immediate VAT clawback, interest at the statutory late-payment rate, and penalties up to 50% of the evaded VAT where abuse or offender intent is found. Knowingly issuing false export declarations or fraudulent e-invoicing may trigger criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment under Luxembourg tax procedural law. Documentary evidence must be retained for at least six years; in the event of export refund audits related to a third-country entity, the AEDV may request additional business-meaning and substance documentation under anti-fraud measures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), Luxembourg's central monetary authority and a member of the Eurosystem; prudential and AML/CFT supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions, and electronic money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, as amended, and CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012. The Ministry of Finance retains policy oversight for foreign-exchange and monetary affairs; neither the BCL nor the CSSF operates a prior-authorisation foreign-exchange control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full euro-area convertibility applies in Luxembourg. Both current-account and capital-account operations are free under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), transposed into Luxembourg law without exchange-control restrictions. There is no requirement to obtain central-bank approval for capital injections, profit distributions, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds of an SCSp. The SCSp is eligible for tax transparency under Luxembourg law, so profits allocated to resident or non-resident limited partners are generally not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax and can be remitted abroad once the partnership accounts evidence the profit allocation. Practical hurdles are documentary and statistical rather than regulatory: credit institutions must complete AML/KYC client files under the amended Law of 12 November 2004, and the BCL requires banks to report cross-border payments and positions in the balance-of-payments statistical framework at the Eurosystem transaction-level threshold (currently EUR 12,500). No capital stay-in, local-investment mandate, convertibility licensing, or repatriation lock-up applies to a revenue-generating MarTech SaaS business held by an SCSp.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation timeline on export receipts, including digital subscription and analytics-licence revenue collected through Stripe, Paddle, or direct SWIFT MT103 credits. Foreign-currency export proceeds may be retained in multi-currency corporate accounts at a Luxembourg credit institution or converted into EUR at freely negotiated commercial rates. The only applicable controls for digital export services are the buyer-side VAT/GST registration rules and the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) filing obligations, neither of which constitutes a foreign-exchange control. Banks may record the underlying commercial invoice for BCL balance-of-payments statistics, but no surrender certificate or BCL clearance is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR, USD, GBP multi-currency) with a linked Capital Escrow Account for investor capital contributions

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (SEPA-capable, euro clearing) and a separate non-interest-bearing Capital Escrow Account
Commercial Operational Account with intraday FX sweep and a Capital Escrow sub-ledger for subscription revenue ring-fencing
Corporate Operational Account with cash concentration and Capital Escrow sub-account
Local Operational Account (EUR) with an optional escrow account for partnership capital calls and distributions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High feasibility for this low AML-risk MarTech SaaS, provided the digital EMI holds an EEA electronic-money institution licence (either Luxembourg-licensed under PSD2 or passported into Luxembourg from another EEA state) and maintains direct participation in SEPA and SEPA Instant clearing. The EMI may open a settlement account in the SCSp's own name even though the SCSp lacks separate legal personality, subject to the general partner's representation and the EMI's acceptance of partnership client structures. Legal and operational constraints: (i) an EMI may not grant credit or pay interest on float, so all working capital must be swept daily to the tier-1 Luxembourg bank account; (ii) Stripe and Paddle are merchant aggregator payment service providers and are not substitutes for a regulated corporate banking relationship; (iii) the EMI must still apply Luxembourg AML/KYC rules, including identification of ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more of the SCSp and verification of the general partner's signatories; (iv) non-EEA or tax-transparent partnership structures may trigger enhanced due diligence and rejection by more conservative EMIs; (v) FX margins at EMIs are generally wider than at tier-1 banks, so the EMI should be used as a collection-only rail, with daily sweeps to a BCL-regulated credit institution for treasury concentration and FX execution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: First-time onboarding at Luxembourg tier-1 banks generally requires a live KYC interview, either physical or validated video-conference, with at least one natural-person director of the general partner and with each direct or indirect limited partner holding 25% or more of the SCSp or its duly authorised delegate. Fully remote documentary-only opening is available only for objectively low-risk cases under CSSF video-identification practice, provided the bank collects high-resolution identity documents, a liveness check, and a recorded interview compliant with Article 3-2(1) of the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing. The SCSp, despite lacking legal personality, may open and operate bank accounts in its own name through its general partner; the partnership agreement and the general partner's board resolution must expressly authorise the opening of bank accounts and grant signature rights. Banks may require the general partner, if a Luxembourg private limited company, to provide its own RBE extract, financial statements, and evidence of substance. In practice, at least one authorised signatory should be an EEA-resident officer to reduce the onboarding timeline; however, remote opening with a qualified electronic signature is commercially achievable for a standard SaaS holding SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp transparency and source-of-funds gap - the bank cannot map the partnership structure, the general partner's authority, or the source of funds of a zero-minimum-capital special limited partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SCSp partnership agreement with all amendments; complete register of limited partners and the general partner; Luxembourg Business Registers RBE extract for the SCSp and the general partner; audited or certified financial statements of each direct corporate investor; source-of-wealth questionnaire and bank reference letter for each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; a written business plan with 24-month cash-flow forecast for the SEO content-analytics platform; confirmation of adherence to CSSF substance expectations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA ownership and cross-border round-tripping suspicion - foreign limited partners and globally distributed SaaS revenue create a red flag that the SCSp is used to circumvent sanctions screening or to layer recurring subscription income.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificates for each non-EEA limited partner and for the general partner; direct and indirect ownership chain chart; sanctions and politically exposed person screening results; merchant-of-record agreements with Stripe and Paddle; sample enterprise customer contracts and platform usage invoices; a geographic breakdown of payment origin and final billing entities; an internal AML assessment of the SaaS commercial model and a signed confirmation that crypto-asset payments and high-risk third-party pass-through payments are not accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Split-payment and structured-transaction concern - recurring small-amount subscription collections can be perceived as smurfing or as an attempt to hide associated transactions below reporting thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and Paddle settlement reports with full transaction trail, refund ledger, and chargeback records; platform usage analytics for key accounts and active users; standard billing policy and EU VAT/OSS treatment of tax invoices; external accountant revenue recognition statement prepared under IFRS 15; an organisational AML risk assessment confirming the Low_Risk_Standard tier for banking_aml_risk_tier; confirmation that all cross-border disbursements are made from the tier-1 Luxembourg bank account and not directly from the merchant aggregator float.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance deficiency - the SCSp uses a registered-office service, has no employees, and the general partner is a management company, indicating a tax-driven shell rather than a commercial enterprise.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office service agreement or lease contract at a Luxembourg business address; substance memorandum demonstrating that strategic decisions of the SCSp are taken in Luxembourg, including general partner board minutes approving the treasury policy, the SaaS commercial contracts, and the appointment of payment processors; sub-contracting agreements with software development and data-labelling teams; evidence of IP ownership, domain registration, and trademark filing for the analytics tool; engagement letters with Luxembourg legal and tax advisers; prior bank statements or audited partnership accounts evidencing real third-party SaaS revenue and operating expenses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Sponsor and investor capital is injected by SWIFT MT103 wire transfer in EUR, USD, or GBP into the SCSp's Capital Escrow Account or dedicated operational account at the Luxembourg tier-1 bank. For EEA resident investors, a SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 purpose code CAPT is the preferred lower-cost rail. For non-EEA investors, the MT103 instruction must include in field 70 the reference to the relevant capital-call article of the partnership agreement and the BCL/Eurosystem balance-of-payments classification for direct-investment equity (EBC class C2 / code C210 or the bank's equivalent BPM6 code), ensuring the receiving bank treats the flow as a capital transaction rather than services or income. The bank will require a signed capital contribution certificate, a partner UBO schedule, and, for non-EEA remitters, source-of-funds documentation before crediting the escrow ledger; funds are normally held in a short pending-capital status pending completion of name screening and compliance checks. USD or GBP inbound amounts may be converted in spot or hedged via an associated FX forward; the exchange rate must be recorded in the SCSp's books to demonstrate transparent capital accounting. No BCL prior authorisation is required, but the bank must report the inflow to the BCL balance-of-payments statistical framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing hierarchy for the MarTech SaaS treasury: (i) SEPA SCT and SEPA Instant for EEA contractors, vendors, payroll, cloud-hosting, and data-licensing costs; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for third-country suppliers, international marketing agencies, and partner distributions, with appropriate ISO 20022 purpose codes such as LICF, ROYL, SUBS, or DIVI, and BIC/IBAN identifiers to avoid screening delays; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 issued by BGL BNP Paribas or BCEE for physical hardware procurement or large-value channel-distribution purchases, although commercially unjustified for a pure SaaS subscription model; (iv) cross-border corporate card programmes (Visa or Mastercard) for digital advertising spend, cloud infrastructure, and Stripe/Paddle platform fees; (v) profit distributions to foreign limited partners executed by SWIFT MT103 with purpose code DIVI, accompanied by the general partner's profit-allocation certificate and a certified copy of the partnership accounts so the payment is characterised as partnership profit rather than director fees or undeclared services. All outbound disbursements must be made from the Luxembourg tier-1 account rather than from the merchant aggregator float, and must satisfy BCL balance-of-payments reporting where the Eurosystem threshold applies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/JPY) executed with a Luxembourg licensed credit institution, tenors from 1 to 12 months, documented under an ISDA/FBF master agreement or standard bank confirmations, and designated as cash-flow hedges of the SCSp's commercial subscription receivables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted emerging-market currencies such as EUR/CNH, EUR/INR, EUR/BRL, and EUR/TRY through the bank's offshore trading desk, used exclusively to hedge local marketing, hosting, and contractor costs.
FX swap combinations (spot/forward and forward/spot) to bridge settlement timing mismatches between Stripe/Paddle collection currencies and EUR operational liquidity requirements.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex, matched to long-term subscription contracts or capital-call funding obligations, with hedge designation confirmed in the SCSp treasury policy.

European-style vanilla FX options (EUR/USD put/call structures) are permissible as a conservative hedge overlay where the general partner has adopted a written FX policy imposing a maximum premium budget; exotic or leveraged structures, including target-redemption forwards and barrier swaps, are prohibited in the SCSp treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Audit Report Deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of partner approval, and in any case no later than seven months after the financial year-end; for calendar-year SCSp entities the statutory filing date is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission triggers a daily administrative penalty (commonly EUR 100 per commenced month) with a statutory cap of EUR 10,000; serious or repeated failure may attract a criminal fine up to EUR 125,000 and, after formal notice, administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Update Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any transfer of partnership interests or change in ultimate beneficial ownership; if no change occurs, an annual no-change confirmation must be submitted through the RBE portal by 31 January of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or confirm accurate UBO data is punishable by administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 per infringement; repeated non-compliance may trigger a formal court rectification order and suspension of profit distributions in an SCSp.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Maintenance Confirmation of Registered Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the initial RCS registration; any change to the general partner, registered office, or commercial object must be filed within one calendar month of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted confirmation may attract an administrative fine of EUR 500; after two consecutive failures the RCS may declare the entity unidentifiable and initiate strike-off proceedings following a 30-day public notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required for a Luxembourg SCSp when two of three thresholds are exceeded: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and 50 full-time employees on average during the financial year. An SCSp below these thresholds qualifies for audit exemption; however, if the SCSp is used as a regulated collective investment vehicle, CSSF rules may nonetheless require a Luxembourg-approved statutory auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) under the Luxembourg law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts or where a lender or investor contractually requires it.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In a Luxembourg SCSp, the general partner is responsible for the beneficial-owner declaration. Each transfer of a partnership interest, pledge, or change in direct or indirect 25%-or-more control must be filed with the RBE within one month and contemporaneously recorded in the internal register. If no such change occurs, an annual no-change confirmation must be submitted by 31 January through the RBE portal, signed by the general partner or an authorised Luxembourg-based professional agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (limited and general partners, participation amounts and classes)
Register of Transfers and Pledges of Partnership Interests
Minute Book of Partner Meetings and General Partner Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,800 per annum for an accredited Luxembourg registered office and corporate secretarial agent (mid-tier corporate service provider quote).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 - USD 15,000 for a full Luxembourg statutory audit; if the SCSp qualifies for audit exemption, the book-review cost may be USD 2,000 - USD 5,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential CIT rate reductions for SaaS analytics companies under standard Luxembourg domestic law; the effective rate is reduced by the full deductibility of the 5% net wealth tax surcharge and municipal business tax deductibility, yielding an aggregate headline CIT plus municipal business tax burden of 24.94% (17% CIT plus 6.75% municipal business tax on taxable income after the 0.60% equalization fund surcharge); additional substance-based IP relief is unavailable absent a qualifying IP box regime election, and the OECD Pillar Two 15% top-up tax applies to Luxembourg constituent entities with annual revenue above the EUR 750 million consolidation threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return form 300 (Formulaire 300) for CIT and municipal business tax; complementary form 307 for VAT if the SCSp exercises the VAT group or registration option; submitted electronically through the Luxembourg tax authority’s MyGuichet.lu and Guichet.lu e-filing portals; form 370 is used for the annual net wealth tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Income tax returns must be filed by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end, or by 31 March of the following year when the return is filed electronically with an approved tax advisor; the administration may grant an extension for Luxembourg parent companies of consolidated groups.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office in Luxembourg, commercial registration number (RCS), and tax file number issued by the Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the SCSp’s Luxembourg registered office and RCS number; use the Luxembourg permanent establishment’s address if the SCSp is managed abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the fiscal period identical to the audited accounts even if the central administration is outside Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Legal form and tax status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the entity form as a special limited partnership (SCSp) and confirmation of transparent tax treatment in Luxembourg.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that non-resident partners are directly assessed for income from the Luxembourg permanent establishment and are not taxed at the partnership level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the taxable net wealth at 31 December, applying the EUR 500,000 wealth tax allowance for commercial entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp is subject to net wealth tax as a taxpayer under the LWTR; liability is limited to the fixed minimum net wealth tax of EUR 535 if the partnership is dormant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pro-rata allocation of the partnership result among direct and indirect partners, including limited partners with negative capital accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a partner allocation schedule; OECD-compliant statements of capital and financing are accepted as supporting detail.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption, dividends received, capital gains on qualified shares, and deductible notional interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the participation exemption only for corporate partners holding at least 10% or an acquisition cost above EUR 1.2 million in qualifying subsidiaries; the exemption does not shelter international portfolio income under a transparent SCSp absent an applicable anti-hybrid analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unilateral credit or deduction for foreign taxes credited to the Luxembourg permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty conditions by jurisdiction and attach Form 303 certification when double tax relief is sought.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a EUR 50 monthly fine for form 300 for taxpayers subject to the simplified filing regime, or 10% of the assessed tax after a formal demand; the assessment becomes final and enforceable if not contested within three months; administrative monetary penalties under article 59 of the Luxembourg tax code range up to EUR 25,000 for willful failure or obstruction, and interest on late tax payments accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum) from the original due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on dividends and profit distributions made by a taxable Luxembourg entity; permanent and transparent SCSp distributions to partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax because the partnership is not a separate taxable person; income reported directly by resident corporate partners may instead be caught by the 15% withholding tax where the payor is a taxable Luxembourg entity, not the SCSp.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke Luxembourg double tax treaty relief on a WHT-liable distribution, the Luxembourg withholding agent must obtain, before the payment date, (i) a valid certificate of tax residence from the partner’s residence state, (ii) a completed Luxembourg annual tax residence certificate where the Luxembourg payer is the beneficiary, and (iii) the OECD exchange of information framework; in practice the payer relies on a self-certification under the EU Savings Directive and the Luxembourg domestic withholding procedure, with protective claims filed with the Luxembourg direct tax administration within the statutory time limit; treaty rates are applied at source or refunded through a formal claim; the reduced rate applies only to the beneficial owner with no Luxembourg permanent establishment effectively connected to the shares.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% withholding tax on outbound royalties under domestic law; a 10% treaty withholding may apply to royalties under several Luxembourg DTA partners, although domestic law exempts royalties from source taxation; interest: domestic 0%; most DTA partners provide 0% withholding on interest, with 10–15% in limited source treaties; neither royalties nor interest arising in the SCSp’s software business will be subject to Luxembourg withholding tax in a well-structured licensing model.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg requires mandatory Local File documentation only when the group has at least 50 employees and either an annual turnover of EUR 10 million or a balance-sheet total above EUR 10 million; full documentation (including Master File) is triggered when the group has at least 250 employees, an annual turnover above EUR 50 million, and a balance-sheet total above EUR 43 million; the Local File threshold is EUR 10 million in annual revenues, which is the relevant trigger for the SCSp’s SEO analytics tool; failure to file the prescribed documentation after formal request triggers a penalty of EUR 2,500 to EUR 25,000 per file, and the tax administration may shift presumptions in transfer pricing adjustments.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not impose separate Economic Substance Regulations in a manner analogous to UAE ESR, but the 2019 Luxembourg tax reform added a substance requirement in articles 168bis and 231 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law, requiring that entities benefiting from tax treaties, participation exemptions, or hybrid mismatch relief maintain locally present personnel, premises, and effective decision-making; the OECD’s substance concept is applied through exchange-of-information rulings and the GAAR under article 6 AbgO, so the SCSp that performs algorithmic content analytics through Luxembourg-based staff and infrastructure will meet the minimum substance threshold, while a pure letterbox company with no local economic activity will be disregarded for treaty purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting from the form 300 the taxable result of the SEO analytics tool, misclassifying taxable international software subscriptions as passive remuneration, or failing to report the Luxembourg permanent establishment of a non-resident partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of the entire concealed tax plus interest at 0.6% per month; a tax adjustment penalty of 10% of the evaded tax or EUR 25,000 for gross negligence; criminal tax fraud is punishable by imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years and a fine of EUR 250 to EUR 50,000 under articles 129 and 130 of the Luxembourg general tax law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners of the SCSp are jointly and severally liable for tax debts of the partnership where they personally participated in the concealment, where the corporate body has been dissolved without sufficient assets, or where the general partner has knowingly organised the false allocation; civil restitution of the tax plus judicial interest, travel bans under criminal procedure, and, in aggravated fraud cases, imprisonment of the natural person up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the ISIC 6201 analytics software only through invoicing entities in no-tax jurisdictions without any Luxembourg staff, contracts, bank decision-making, or technical development, or using the SCSp as the sole conduit for profit repatriation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disapplication of treaty benefits under the principal purpose test of the Multilateral Convention (BEPS MLI), reclassification of the entire subscription stream as Luxembourg-source income, a 10% gross-up assessment, and fines under article 6 AbgO for abusive tax structures; civil penalties up to EUR 25,000 and refusal of the territorial advance tax ruling.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or general partner who signs the annual accounts knowing that the partnership lacks substance may be personally assessed for the additional tax as a representative taxpayer, ordered to restore the funds distributed on a sham basis, and be subjected to a five-year directorship ban in Luxembourg if the filing was made in bad faith.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the special limited partnership to receive Stripe or Paddle subscription proceeds from non-transparent e-commerce flows, failing to identify the beneficial owner in the beneficial ownership register, and failing to file suspicious-transaction reports with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit while executing PE-owned client contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Luxembourg AML law of up to EUR 1 million for legal persons and EUR 125,000 for responsible officers per breach; the Luxembourg regulator may suspend the professional activity and the Commercial Register may order the dissolution of the vehicle; the court may impose a criminal fine up to EUR 5 million for breach of the law of 12 November 2004 as amended.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are personally liable for deliberate or seriously negligent AML failures, are disqualified from serving as a manager in any Luxembourg financial entity, and may be sentenced to imprisonment of up to five years where the partnership is found to be an instrument for laundering the proceeds of illegal SEO/content-fraud activities.
